targetAudience.primary: Engineering leads and governance owners designing digital-employee escalation systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands agent routing, confidence scores, and resource budgets.
targetAudience.readerProblem: One confidence score is being used to detect failure, choose a collaboration topology, and authorize cost.

whyNow: A controlled cost-aware multi-agent routing study separates strong baseline-failure prediction from much weaker protocol-specific value prediction while recording materially different token costs.

externalHook.description: Matched outcomes show that knowing an answer is risky is easier than knowing which collaboration protocol will add enough value.

coreProposition: Failure-risk admission, protocol-specific value, and budget admission are separate evidence decisions: detecting likely failure does not select a collaboration topology, and selecting a topology does not authorize its cost.

originalValue.description: Separates failure-risk admission, protocol-value routing, and budget admission so each failure class remains auditable.

readerTakeaway: Open escalation consideration with risk evidence, rank named protocols with protocol-specific evidence, and authorize the selected cost through a separate budget policy.

supported: The selected study reports strong post-answer baseline-failure discrimination in its matched OmniMath setting.
The same study reports much weaker protocol-specific value prediction and material token-cost differences.
The evidence supports separating risk detection, topology choice, and budget authority.
unsupported: A deployable pre-execution router with the reported post-answer performance
Product pricing from study token counts
uncertain: Which production-time features predict protocol-specific value without leakage
How latency, tool calls, and human review should enter budget admission

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument is derived from public primary research and remains independently useful.

decisionReason: The evidence supports a bounded, actionable escalation-governance model without claiming universal protocol superiority.
